emerging_technology: Agentic AI using an LLM to coordinate retrieval and reconciliation tools
intended_application: Freight-invoice reconciliation: retrieve invoices, shipment and rate records, flag discrepancies and draft recommendations; humans retain payment authority.
business_need: Reduce reconciliation effort and improve exception handling without weakening payment controls.
users_stakeholders: Accounts payable (AP), freight operations, controller, IT/security, carriers and customers
adoption_posture: Moderate fast-follower; willing to test a bounded reversible pilot
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect matching or unsupported recommendations could cause duplicate or incorrect payments and expose commercial data. No agent payment approval or release is permitted.
management_question: Is the organization ready for a human-reviewed pilot, and what must change before starting and sustaining it?
time_horizon: Prepare over the next 90 days; production requires a separate decision.
capabilities_constraints:
H-L [leadership/sponsorship]: COO and controller signed the pilot charter and decision rights.
H-S [skills]: AP reviewers and integration/security engineers completed scenario-based evaluation and incident training.
H-W [workflow/process]: Exception queues, staffed human review and manual fallback were rehearsed on representative cases.
H-D [infrastructure/data]: Versioned invoice/rate/shipment samples have reconciled identifiers and provenance; scoped read-only access tests passed.
H-R [resources/budget]: Pilot reviewers, training and ongoing support have approved staffing and budget.
H-G [governance/risk]: Read-only permissions deny payment writes; controller approval remains external; logging and stop/incident drills passed.
H-C [culture/change]: AP representatives co-designed the workflow; feedback and role-change communication are in place.
H-O [operating ownership]: AP director is named accountable owner; IT service lead covers support and the escalation rota is rehearsed.
